tagline: Along the Sacramento River levees, bridge by bridge to the capital.
intro: From the Antioch Bridge, Highway 160 crosses Sherman Island and takes to the east levee of the Sacramento River, and all the way to Sacramento it stays near the water. It crosses Three Mile Slough on a 1949 lift bridge, passes Rio Vista and Isleton, and changes banks and islands on a run of drawbridges before the last levee into the city.

The bascule bridges at Isleton and Paintersville replaced free ferries in 1923, built to a type patented by Joseph Strauss, who went on to design the Golden Gate Bridge. The year before, the Victory Highway Association chose this river road, promoted locally as the Netherlands of America, for its route to the bay.

moments.title: Isleton
moments.text: Josiah Poole founded the town in 1874 and built a wharf, then moved out after the floods of 1878 and 1881. Some of the old storefronts on the main street show a Chinese hand.

moments.title: Locke
moments.text: A 14-acre town that grew after a 1915 fire burned the Chinatown in Walnut Grove, a mile south. It is a National Historic Landmark for its Chinese American rural life.

moments.title: Courtland
moments.text: Named for Courtland Sims, son of the landowner who opened a steamer landing here in 1870.
